author: rdc-rfc1-author-a (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: rst_sync[1] is the only clk_b stage and samples rst_sync[0], which changes on clk_a. It releases q directly, so the clk_b release can be metastable.

author_reading.rationale: The first synchroniser stage is clocked by clk_a while the second stage and the functional flops run on clk_b, so the release is not resolved in the clk_b domain.

labels.rationale: The release chain has its first stage on clk_a and its second on clk_b. The clk_b flop samples an asynchronous clk_a signal with no clk_b stage behind it, so it is effectively a one-stage synchroniser in clk_b. q is released from that flop, which can be metastable.
The first stage launches on clk_a, making rst_sync[1] the first clk_b sampler of an asynchronous transition. That same stage directly releases the downstream reset.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on bad, critical and the class. RDC-003 (unrecognised chain in the receiving domain) and RDC-014 (reset driven by a register that is not a recognised synchroniser) both target this release. RDC-002 and CDC-003 (B) are incidental or outside the RDC deck. The settler rewrote the line 1 comment, which named the defect.
